title: Small-batch penalty investigation: timeout vs fairness tradeoffs
body:
Background:

Quick notes: we see regular p99 spikes on low-concurrency customers. Hypothesis: tiny batches (1-3 requests) cause an inefficiency penalty that increases tail latency due to kernel launch, memory copy overhead, and poor GPU occupancy; in addition, fairness heuristics that demote ‘aggressive’ pipelines can interact with timeouts to create starvation pockets.

Goal:
- Quantify the performance penalty per-request for small batches across representative models (gpt-medium, llama-3-7B, redwood-v1-small) and sequence lengths (64, 256, 1024).
- Understand how scheduler timeout values and fairness demotion thresholds affect p50/p95/p99 and throughput.
- Identify concrete mitigations (timeout tuning, micro-batching, prefetch, KV-cache warm policies).

High-level hypotheses:
1) There is a non-linear penalty for very small batches: overhead dominates at batch sizes <= 4.
2) Increasing the batching timeout reduces penalty but increases median latency; there's a sweet spot that minimizes p99 under mixed loads.
3) Fairness demotion (age-based priority lowering) can cause trailing requests to starve and exacerbate p99 when microbursts are present.

Experiment design:
- Controlled driver that replays production arrival traces (sampled from customer cluster X on 2025-07-21). Two workload modes: steady (Poisson) and bursty (peaky with 100ms microbursts).
- Model configurations: 3 models, each pinned to a single GPU to isolate kernel effects.
- Queueing configs sweep: timeout = [1ms, 2ms, 5ms, 10ms, 20ms, 50ms]; max_batch = [4,8,16,32]; fairness: on/off; age-demote-threshold = [50ms, 100ms, 200ms].
- Measurement: client-side latency (end-to-end), scheduler trace (enqueue->dispatch), GPU occupancy (nvidia-smi sampling + CUPTI heatmap), kernel timing (host+device), KV-cache hit rates, RPC serialization time.
- Repeats: 10 runs per config, 95% CI reported.

Quick instrumentation notes (how we measured):
- Scheduler timestamps added at enqueue, batch-formation, flush, dispatch, kernel-start, kernel-end, response-serialize.
- Tracing collection via jaeger + local microtrace collector for high-resolution timestamps.
- GPU metrics: CUPTI traces for kernel launch + runtime occupancy snapshots every 10ms; fallback to nvprof in one-off runs.

Raw observations (selected):
- For gpt-medium, seq=256: batch=1 p50=18ms, p95=112ms, p99=284ms. batch=8 p50=22ms, p95=78ms, p99=105ms. Means: median shifts up slightly but tail collapses with larger batches.
- Kernel launch overhead measured ~0.9-1.5ms per kernel for llama-3-7B on our runtime (includes small memcpy and kernel enqueue).
- For small batches GPU occupancy < 25% (profiler). For batch >=16 occupancy ~62%.
- Unexpected: serialization + RPC stack added ~2.5ms variance that compounds for tiny batches; when we disabled certain tracing layers, p99 improved ~6% on small batches.

Timeout sweep notes:
- timeout=1-2ms: very low median but extreme p99 blowups in bursty traces (observed 2.5x p99 vs timeout=10ms). Likely cause: flurries create many tiny batches that consume slots and push other requests into new batches repeatedly, increasing age for some requests due to demotion rules.
- timeout=20-50ms: smoother tails but throughput drops ~6-10% because we wait longer to fill batches; for latency-sensitive SLAs this is borderline.
- Sweet spot for mixed workloads observed around 5-10ms for most models. This balancing point minimized p99 while keeping p50 acceptable.

Fairness interaction notes:
- Age-based demotion: when enabled at 100ms it prevented hot tenants from monopolizing slots but also demoted some older requests into lower priority queues which then experienced >200ms extra delay in certain overloaded windows.
- When fairness off, heavy clients could saturate slots leading to higher p99 for smaller clients. No win without tradeoff.
- Proposed tweak: soft-demote with backoff window + a micro-burst recovery token bucket to allow occasional fast-path for demoted requests.

Profiling bottlenecks and root-cause hypotheses:
- Kernel launch + memcpy latency is fixed per-batch; dominates for tiny batches. Mitigation: micro-batching within the runtime (coalesce two logically-separate requests into one kernel call when semantically safe) and minimize memcpy via zero-copy paths for small payloads.
- Scheduler contention: lock contention seen in the batch-formation path under extreme bursts (hotspot around queue head lock). Fix: sharded queues or lock-free ring buffers.
- KV-cache cold misses: when many small requests reference different prefixes, KV cache thrash increases per-token compute; observed higher per-token time for tiny batches with random-prefix distribution. Mitigation: eviction tuning, prefetch heuristics for common prefixes.

Representative numbers (gpt-medium, mix bursty load):
- Config A (timeout=2ms, max_batch=8, fairness=on(100ms)): throughput=460 req/s, p50=24ms, p95=96ms, p99=214ms
- Config B (timeout=10ms, max_batch=16, fairness=on(100ms)): throughput=420 req/s, p50=38ms, p95=72ms, p99=92ms
- Config C (timeout=5ms, max_batch=8, fairness=off): throughput=500 req/s, p50=18ms, p95=110ms, p99=260ms
Interpretation: Config B is best for p99 at modest throughput; Config C maximizes throughput but with worst tail.

Diagnostics artifacts (links to traces/logs):
- High-res trace (run 2025-07-28): trace id run-20250728-0929 (internal link in tracing dashboard)
- CUPTI kernel map: s3://redwood-prod-traces/serving-runtime/batch-penalty/2025-07-28/cupti-map.gz
- Scheduler flamegraph: https://internal-tools/redwood/flamegraph/serving-runtime/penalty-20250728

Mitigations tested (quick):
1) Microbatch coalescer prototype (coalesce window 1ms): reduced p99 by ~18% for small batches but added complexity around token budgets. PR: linked above.
2) Soft-demote change: instead of immediate demote, we mark candidate and allow 2x quick-paths if waiting > 120ms. Reduced starvation cases by ~65%.
3) Serialization fast-path (zero-copy for small payloads): reduced end-to-end variance by ~10% and p99 by ~6% in tiny-batch runs.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need a formal cost model that maps kernel-launch overhead vs filling timeout to customer economics (cost per token under SLA).
- Evaluate microbatch coalescer under multi-model co-location (safety: mixing model states).
- More runs on Llama-3-7B with long sequences (>=1024) to measure when token compute starts to dominate overhead.
- Decide default timeout change for Hosted API (optimize p99 for free-tier vs throughput for enterprise).
- Add an automated daily probe that runs a synthetic microburst trace and records p99 for key models.

Action items (owner assignments):
- Diego: finish microbatch coalescer integration tests + expand test matrices to multi-tenant co-location (due 2025-08-17).
- Priya: build cost model spreadsheet and simulate SLA scenarios (due 2025-08-14).
- Tomáš: prototype sharded queue rewrite for batch-formation path, measure lock contention (due 2025-09-01).
- Ava: follow up on Hosted API default change decision, coordinate with product for rollout notes (due 2025-08-21).

Notes to self:
- Keep an eye on NVLINK memcpy behavior on A100 vs H100; observed slightly different kernel enqueue timings between hardware.
